ahem... I hawk this add-on any chance I get. It installs with pretty tame restrictions, but I have mine set to super-uber-serious-guise mode. Originally found it specifically because of browser fingerprinting.

It spoofs (and randomizes, given customizable intervals) everything: the browser, OS, timezone, IP address, screen-resolution, etc. Everything else is blocked on mine: uses system fonts and disables access to the font folder, disables referrers, etc + a whole bunch of others settings that are too numerous to mention here.

Keep in mind, it breaks a lot of sites. But you can whitelist the ones you trust, and temporarily disable only certain features if you really need to (disabling referrers kills download links, on some sites). Honestly, it's kind of annoying, at first. But you get used to it after a while; I've ran plenty of exploit-testing sites, and not one has managed to identify me.
